forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.previous_feedback: Keep the identity R_{a,b,r}(q) = [r+a+b choose b]_q / [r+a+b choose a]_q if useful, but do NOT invoke the root positivity theorem or the stronger ancestor positivity lemma. You need an independent argument from the assumption R_{a,b,r}(q) \in Z[q] to the claimed lower-half coefficient nonnegativity. In particular: (1) retain the q-factorial manipulation only as an algebraic rewrite; (2) prove the needed coefficient statement directly from the product/ratio structure or via a separately established non-circular sublemma; (3) conclude only the target range 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), not by appealing to a forbidden all-coefficients theorem.
payload.previous_proof_nl:
Let N := r+a+b. Since 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, we have N >= b >= a >= 0; in particular 0 <= a <= N and 0 <= b <= N, and also N-a = r+b >= 0 and N-b = r+a >= 0. By the standard polynomial form of Gaussian q-binomial coefficients, for 0 <= t <= N one has [N choose t]_q = (q;q)_N / ((q;q)_t (q;q)_{N-t}). Therefore
[N choose b]_q / [N choose a]_q = ((q;q)_N / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{N-b})) / ((q;q)_N / ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{N-a})) = ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{N-a}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{N-b}).
Using N-a = r+b and N-b = r+a, this becomes
[N choose b]_q / [N choose a]_q = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b) = R_{a,b,r}(q).
Thus R_{a,b,r}(q) is exactly a quotient of two Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. By hypothesis R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q], so this quotient is a polynomial in q. Applying the allowed semantic anchor with n = N, k = b, and l = a, we conclude that every coefficient of R_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative. Since R_{a,b,r}(q) is in Z[q], all of its coefficients are integers. Therefore, for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer. This proves the lemma.
